title: 04 Quadratics Multiplying and factoring: Visual Guide
outline: Title: 04 Quadratics Multiplying and factoring: Visual Guide

1. Expand And Undo | a 2-by-2 area box for (x+p)(x+q) with draggable p and q, the four partial products, the collapsed trinomial, and the factor-pair search that reads the same box right to left | multiplying binomials is the distributive law twice, so the middle coefficient is the SUM p+q and the constant is the PRODUCT pq; factoring is that box read backwards, which is why expanding your answer proves it

2. The Middle Term | three special products chosen by a segmented control, with a and b sliders driving an area dissection - the square of a sum split into a^2, two ab strips and b^2, the square of a difference as strips removed and a corner added back, and the difference of squares as two cross terms cancelling | (a+b)^2 = a^2+2ab+b^2 and (a-b)^2 = a^2-2ab+b^2 differ only in the middle sign while the last term stays positive, and (a+b)(a-b) = a^2-b^2 is the only one whose middle term vanishes; omitting 2ab is the classic error and coefficients get squared too, so (2x+1)(2x-1) = 4x^2-1

3. Spot The Pattern | three sliders build any Ax^2+Bx+C and the panel runs the real decision procedure live - greatest common factor, term count, then difference of squares, sum of squares, perfect square trinomial or a factor-pair search - with quiz presets from x^2-9 to 2x^2-18 | check the GCF first and then count terms; two terms and a minus with both pieces square is a difference of squares, three terms passing the 2ab middle-term test is a perfect square, and x^2+9 is a sum of squares that does not factor over the reals

4. Group And Factor | a four-term polynomial kx^3+kpx^2+kqx+kpq built from three sliders, shown as coloured pair chips, with a switch between the pairing that works and the pairing that dead-ends, plus the expand-back check | grouping is the GCF move applied three times, and it only closes when both pairs leave the SAME bracket - mismatched brackets mean the pairing was wrong, not that the polynomial is unfactorable, as x^3+3x^2+2x+6 = (x+3)(x^2+2) shows
